newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines fires warning shots at Chinese boats.
newsitem.headline: Philippines fires warning shots at Chinese boats.

text.p: Philippine troops fired warning shots to drive away Chinese fishing boats in the latest incident involving the two countries in the disputed Spratly Islands, the military said on Tuesday.
A military report said the shooting was on Friday after a Chinese fishing vessel anchored near Philippine-occupied Kota Island and sent five boats to fish in the area.
"This prompted Kota detachment to give warning shots, forcing them to stop their activities and (they) immediately went back to their mother ship," said the report released to reporters.
The mother vessel withdrew two hours later, it said.
Defence Secretary Renato de Villa played down the incident as "really nothing serious" and said the military was investigating.
"It seems that some guards on the island...allegedly fired small arms, warning shots into the air," he said, adding that "nobody got hurt and nobody complained about it".
There was no immediate reaction from the Chinese embassy. An employee said the embassy spokesman was out and no one else was authorised to comment.
The Spratlys are a cluster of islets, reefs and shoals in the South China Sea which are believed to be potentially rich in oil and natural gas.
Beijing says everything in the sea historically belongs to China. The Spratlys are also claimed wholly or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
Tension flared in April when Manila accused Beijing of sending armed naval ships near two islands occupied by Filipinos.

Beijing in turn accused Manila of violating Chinese sovereignty after Filipinos hoisted their flag over a rocky outcrop called Scarborough Shoal, also in the South China Sea but well north of the Spratlys.

Relations were further strained last month when a Philippine navy ship arrested 21 Chinese fishermen near the shoal and rejected Chinese demands for their release. Beijing said the fishermen were in a territory that has belonged to China for 700 years.
The Chinese are now facing charges of illegal entry.

The military has reported increasing Chinese fishing activity in the Manila-claimed area. On the same day the Chinese were driven away from Kota, two Chinese fishing boats were seen near two other Filipino-held islets, the military said.
